correctness.rationale: For every nonconstant real vector x, sorting or nested layer-cake cuts gives sharp (n−1)D(x)≤G(x)≤floor(n²/4)D(x), with singleton and balanced binary cuts saturating. Both induced operator inequalities immediately follow for row-stochastic P on the constant quotient. The Dobrushin row-L1/2 formula holds by optimizing over [0,1]^n. Rank-one P=J+(4n)^{-1}uv^T with zero-sum u,v is strictly positive bistochastic, and its exact δ and γ factor into primal/dual cut seminorms; two explicit choices independently attain c_n and 1/c_n for all n≥2. Independent exact rational binary-cut tests for n=2..8 confirm both families; n4 symmetric positive-semidefinite Laplacian perturbations give γ(B+)=10/3 vs δ(B+)=3 and γ(B−)=7/2 vs δ(B−)=4, yielding both strict orderings, while c_n=1 for n2,3. Finite tests corroborate the all-n proof rather than extrapolate it.
residual_risks: Saturated constants not claimed best among symmetric/reversible subset; one-step, real, complete-pair unweighted Gini only.

value.rationale: Sharp equivalence between two natural finite-state Markov contraction metrics matters because Gini measures all-pair signal disagreement while Dobrushin measures worst-pair spread. The sharp loss grows linearly with states despite strictly positive bistochastic mixing, and even reversible PSD Markov chains reverse which coefficient is larger at the first possible size. This structural difference and extremal witnesses provide meaningful dimension-dependent insight beyond copying a textbook seminorm inequality.
residual_risks: Main inequality alone is elementary norm equivalence; the distinctive substantive finding is strong-class sharpness and reversed reversible rankings, subject to older-norm literature priority risk.
